podcast_name: Systemise and Scale with Gary Das
episode_title: Why More Leads Will Make Things Worse | Ep 440
question: What is the £100,000 per head revenue rule for scaling a mortgage business?
transcript_excerpt: The rule of thumb is that you should aim for £100,000 pounds per head revenue. As one person, you want to try and get to £100,000. As two people, you want to try and get to £200,000. If you have two part-time people, that's one full-time person. When you've got three, that is £200,000. If you're a team of 10 and you're not doing at least a million pounds per year, you need to fix your leaky bucket and get your team working more efficiently.

question: Why did Empire Mortgages double revenue by hiring an admin instead of another advisor?
transcript_excerpt: Empire Mortgages had their biggest single change when they thought they needed another advisor. Instead, Gary helped them recruit another admin, and they wrote an additional £60,000 within 90 days, effectively doubling their business just by making one transactional shift. They weren't paying away 50% in commission; they were just paying for a salary to manage the £10 tasks.

podcast_name: Systemise and Scale with Gary Das
episode_title: Why More Leads Will Make Things Worse | Ep 440
question: How should you track your time before hiring your first team member?
transcript_excerpt: Before you hire anyone, you need to track every hour for at least two weeks using a spreadsheet that runs from 8 AM until whatever time you finish (like 8 PM for 12-hour days). You go through and work out exactly what you're doing in half-hour or hour increments throughout that whole two-week period, putting things into four buckets: new business, advice, post-sale application, and working on the business. The highest value activity is working on your business, while the other three buckets are the ones eating you alive.

question: What is the solo mortgage advisor revenue capacity limit before needing to hire?
transcript_excerpt: If you are a solo person right now, you're probably capped around about £75,000, maybe £60,000 to £100,000 depending on the type of client. If you're really good at selling protection or maximizing client value, you'll probably be pushing higher up towards £100,000. If you're dealing with million-pound mortgages, it's easier to hit that cap.

podcast_name: Systemise and Scale with Gary Das
episode_title: Why More Leads Will Make Things Worse | Ep 440
question: What are the three questions to ask before hiring your first admin or advisor?
transcript_excerpt: Number one, can you afford it based on the written business that you've done over the last three months? Number two, will it free up the time that earns more money—like if you've got protection sitting on your desk or if you're doing too much administration? And number three, have the role written down in specific tasks, actions, and techniques that you want them to put into place. That is vital.
